units.text: INT. GARAGE APARTMENT - AFTERNOON
A converted garage with a low ceiling and one window the size of a cereal box.
Cardboard and plastic bags of hardware cover the floor.
A half-built bunk bed frame lies on its side like a patient.
LUCIANO FERRARI, forties, sleeves rolled, kneels over an instruction sheet that has no words, only drawings.
His wife MARISOL FERRARI, forties, sits cross-legged holding a hex key and a juice box.
Their daughter PIP, nine, sorts bolts into a muffin tin.
Their son TOMASZ, fifteen, leans on the doorframe with earbuds in one ear.
Okay, everybody. Step four. Step four is the ladder.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: I thought step four was the guard rail.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Step four is the ladder. Step five is the guard rail.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Papa, there are two step fours.
units.name: PIP

units.text: He turns the sheet over.
Then back.
There are two step fours.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Pip, how many bolts do we have of the long kind?
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Eleven. The directions say twelve.
units.name: PIP

units.text: So we're one short, which means we've been doing it wrong the whole time.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Tomasz, go outside and breathe.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: I'm literally just standing here.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Tommy, would you hold this end?
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: He pulls out the earbud and takes the rail.
She slides a peg into a hole.
It fits with a soft click.
Look at that.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Beginner's luck.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Papa, I heard that.
units.name: PIP

units.text: You were supposed to.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: He picks up the long bolt he thought was missing from under the instruction sheet and holds it up like a prize.
Twelve.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Told you it was somewhere.
units.name: PIP

units.text: You said eleven.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Eleven in the tin. Twelve in the universe.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Marisol laughs into her juice box.
Luciano tightens the bolt with the key, a careful quarter turn at a time.
Everyone hold your end. On three. One, two...
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: The frame lifts.
It stands.
It wobbles a little and settles.
Well. It's a bed.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: It's crooked.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: It's a crooked bed. It's ours.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Who gets the top?
units.name: PIP

units.text: Obviously me.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Obviously not.
units.name: PIP

units.text: We'll flip for it later. Right now, who's hungry?
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: Dinner is whoever can find the pot with the lid.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: Nobody moves.
Pip returns to the muffin tin and pushes the bolts around with one finger.
I hope I get the bottom.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Tomasz hears.
He says nothing, but he sits on the lower mattress and bounces once, testing it, then pats the top one with his palm as if saying goodnight.
Fine. I'll take the top. For the exercise.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Thanks, Tommy.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Don't make it weird.
units.name: TOMASZ

units.text: Luciano sets down the key and sits on the floor with his back against the frame, looking at the crooked ceiling.
Marisol. We have a house with a ladder now.
units.name: LUCIANO

units.text: We have a house with two step fours.
units.name: MARISOL

units.text: She leans her head on his shoulder.
The window light slides a few inches across the floor.
